variants.name: Scala 3 enum with cases
variants.implementation_notes: Scala 3's enum gives a closed set whose values are members of the enum type: cases are defined in the companion and valueOf/values/fromOrdinal are generated. Pattern matches over the enum are checked for exhaustiveness by the compiler, which is the realization of the pattern's closure; cases may carry parameters or extend java.lang.Enum for Java interop. Unlike case objects, plain enum cases widen to the enum type, which keeps type inference predictable.
variants.code_sketch:
enum Suit(val key: String):
  case Clubs    extends Suit("clubs")
  case Diamonds extends Suit("diamonds")
  case Hearts   extends Suit("hearts")
  case Spades   extends Suit("spades")

Suit.values.toList          // all members, in declaration order
Suit.valueOf("Clubs")       // parse by name; throws on unknown
val s: Suit = Suit.Clubs    // no Int/String converts in
pitfalls: Exhaustiveness warnings must be fatal (-Xfatal-warnings) or they are only a hint in most builds.
values/fromOrdinal exist but ordinals are declaration order; use the key field for persistence.
Extending java.lang.Enum for interop changes name/toString semantics and pulls in Java enum behaviour.

variants.name: Scala 2 sealed trait + case objects
variants.idiom_name: sealed trait/abstract class with case object members
variants.implementation_notes: The Scala 2 encoding: a sealed base trait or abstract class plus one case object per member. Sealing confines extension to the same file, which is what lets the compiler check matches for exhaustiveness; case objects provide structural equals/hashCode/toString. This remains a legitimate realization in Scala 3 projects that have not migrated. Scala 2's own scala.Enumeration (values/Value) is discouraged and should not be used.
pitfalls: Omitting `sealed` removes exhaustiveness checking entirely: the match compiles and fails at run time with MatchError.
Case objects have singleton types, so containers of case objects infer precise singleton types and can break implicit resolution that expects the enum type (scala/scala3#23558).
No iteration or name lookup is generated: values/toList/valueOf must be written by hand (a widely used pattern, but easy to let drift).
